_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Both edits are applied by the factory's overlay.sh (~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/google-workspace/overlay.sh) after every generate. The multi-client tenant layer (gws_tenants.go, gws_tenants_cmd.go, gws_fanout.go and the novel report commands) is NOVEL and wires in through the generator's own hook points (registerNovelCommand, registerClientHook, config.StoreScopeIdentity), so regen-merge keeps it without a ledger entry.

handfixes.summary: helpers.go no longer defines retainCLIQueryParams / retainExplicitQueryParams
handfixes.why: The press 4.33 template emits both helpers for paginated generated callers, but a Google Discovery-sourced spec produces no generated caller that uses them, so they ship as dead code and the press's dogfood dead-helper check FAILs the build. The factory's overlay.sh deletes both function bodies after generate; a reprint re-emits them and dogfood/shipcheck fail again. Only a comment in paginatedGet still names retainCLIQueryParams, which is why the asserts pin the func declarations, not the bare name.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: only emit retainCLIQueryParams/retainExplicitQueryParams when at least one generated command calls them (Discovery-spec prints never do). Filed in the google-workspace press retro notes (~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/google-workspace/FACTORY.md).

handfixes.summary: Reseller and Licensing MCP tool paths are absolute URLs (https://reseller.googleapis.com, https://licensing.googleapis.com), matching resource_paths.go and the MCP code-orchestration table
handfixes.why: This print merges five Google APIs on three hosts. The press's multi-host merge records Reseller and Licensing tools in tools-manifest.json HOST-RELATIVE (/apps/reseller/..., /apps/licensing/...) while resource_paths.go and internal/mcp/code_orch.go carry them absolute; a relative path resolves against the default admin.googleapis.com host, which serves neither API, and press verify's resource-path contract check flags tail/export/import as 3 critical. overlay.sh rewrites the tools-manifest.json paths to absolute, and `lock promote` reverted them once, so the fix has to be re-applied after every promote. tools-manifest.json itself is a library artifact that onboarding does not vendor into this directory, so the asserts below pin the vendored twins it must agree with: if a reprint ever makes the code-orch table or resource paths host-relative as well, the Reseller and Licensing MCP tools would call the wrong host. The code_orch.go asserts pin the executable Path fields themselves (17 Reseller, 7 Licensing endpoints); the same URLs also appear in search keywords, which an earlier, looser assert counted by mistake.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the multi-host merge should record every non-default-host tool path absolute in tools-manifest.json, the same way resource_paths.go already does, and lock promote must not regenerate it host-relative.

handfixes.summary: Group and member command Examples and pp:happy-args use the group email sales@example.com instead of the factory's invented group ID 03x8tuzt3hqdv5v
handfixes.why: The factory's curate-spec.sh feeds ID-form example hints into generation because the Discovery generator rejects '@' in example values; for groupKey it invented 03x8tuzt3hqdv5v. In 13 generated files that value sits in the pp:happy-args annotation as the value of the groupKey happy-arg, and gitleaks' default generic-api-key rule matches that pairing (a *Key= keyword followed by a high-entropy token), so the repo's CI secret scan fails the guards job on a fake ID. Google's groupKey accepts a group email, so the example now uses sales@example.com, which is a valid groupKey and does not match the rule. A reprint re-emits the invented ID.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Factory-side: change the groupKey hint in ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/google-workspace/curate-spec.sh to a low-entropy value, or teach the press's descriptionExampleValue to accept email-shaped examples (the '@' rejection is already in the google-workspace press retro notes).

handfixes.summary: getenvTenant reads GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_TENANT through cliutil.EnvOverride, so an unset .mcpb field is no tenant rather than a tenant named ${user_config.google_workspace_tenant}
handfixes.why: manifest.json maps GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_TENANT to ${user_config.google_workspace_tenant}, and an MCPB host that skips an optional field leaves that template text in the environment (the binary's own cliutil.EnvOverride contract). The factory's tenant layer read it with raw os.Getenv, so a blank 'Default client tenant' made every tool call without an explicit tenant fail 'unknown tenant', including the raw-endpoint execute tool, which has no tenant argument. Found by the onboard adversarial review (round 1, P1). gws_tenants.go is a NOVEL file carried from the factory's novel/ directory, so a re-onboard from that source would bring the raw read back.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Factory-side: apply the same one-line change to ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/google-workspace/novel/gws_tenants.go and the library copy so the next print carries it.

handfixes.summary: offboard's follow-up hints name license-assignments delete per held licence and omit --tenant for the implicit single-org tenant
handfixes.why: When a Drive/Calendar transfer is pending, offboard skips licence release and prints a follow-up. The factory version printed 'offboard <email> --tenant <t> --release-license --keep-groups --yes', which (a) in single-org bearer mode named the implicit tenant 'default', which is not a registry entry, so it exited 2, and (b) re-ran the backup-code and token steps against the now-suspended account, where Google rejects them, so it ended exit 5 even after releasing the licence. The hint now lists one 'license-assignments delete <skuId> <email> --product-id <productId>' per held licence, and tenantArg() drops --tenant when the tenant has no key file. Found by the onboard adversarial review (round 1, P1).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Factory-side: port licenseReleaseHints/tenantArg into ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/google-workspace/novel/ (offboard.go) and the library copy.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real argument-free GET with the client's credential (the tenant-minted token or the single-org bearer) and reports a 404 as a wrong base_url, instead of 'present, not verified' and 'reachable (HTML body at /)'
handfixes.why: Same fleet defect as issue #282, gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py: as printed by press 4.33.5, doctor never probed the credential ('present, not verified') and called any answer at / reachable, so a working install, an expired credential and a wrong base_url produced the same report. Ported the fleet's doctor_verdict.go (doctorReadProbe, doctorProbeableLeaf, doctorProbeCredentials, doctorWrongBaseURL); 4.33.5 already emits doctorBaseURLIsPlaceholder and Client.ProbeGet natively, so those are not duplicated. The probe asks the CLIENT for its credential because a registered tenant's token is minted by the client hook into the client's config, never into the config doctor loads.

asserts.not_contains: present, not verified. Run `%s %s` to confirm the token works end-to-end.

handfixes.summary: sync pages every synced resource (applications, groups, subscriptions, transfers, users) with pageToken/nextPageToken instead of reading one page and recording the resource complete
handfixes.why: The Discovery-sourced print emitted empty determinePaginationDefaults/resourceSupportsPagination switches, so `sync` sent no maxResults/pageToken, stored the first page (100 users on Google's default), and reported success: a tenant with 150 users mirrored 100 with no truncation warning, and search/analytics then answered from an incomplete mirror. Measured against a two-page stub: 100 records before, 150 after. Found by the onboard Codex review (P1). Every synced list method declares pageToken and maxResults in Google's Discovery docs; 100 is within each method's maxResults cap (users 500, groups 200, data-transfer applications/transfers 500, reseller subscriptions 100).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the googlediscovery profiler should populate the pagination tables from Discovery's pageToken/maxResults parameters and the response schema's nextPageToken.

handfixes.summary: The MCP google-workspace_execute tool substitutes every {name} left in an endpoint path from the call's params, not only the endpoint's positional arguments
handfixes.why: The Discovery print binds some path variables as CLI flags (customerKey, customer and similar), so they never appear in the code-orchestration table's Positional list, and execute only substituted Positional names: `customers.get` with params {customerKey: my_customer} failed 'unresolved path parameter {customerKey}' (Codex counted 77 such endpoints). codeOrchBindRemainingPathVars now binds any remaining {name} supplied in params (path-escaped) and removes it from params; an unsupplied variable still fails clearly in the client. Found by the onboard Codex review (P1); receipt: the call now reaches GET /admin/directory/v1/customers/my_customer. The call-site test (TestCodeOrchExecuteBindsFlagBoundPathVar) fails with the guard removed; the helper-only test does not.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit a TemplateParams/Positional binding for every path variable in the code-orchestration table, including ones the CLI exposes as flags with defaults.

handfixes.summary: When a registered tenant is selected, the local store never adopts the store file named for an ambient bearer token
handfixes.why: The store is keyed to 'tenant:<name>' when a tenant is selected, but configureDefaultDBScope still passed the config's bearer credential (GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_TOKEN, ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN or an auth set-token value, i.e. some other organization) as the 'legacy' identity, and defaultDBPathInDir renames a legacy-named store onto the current one. An MSP who synced their own org in bearer mode and later ran --tenant acme with the token still set would have their own org's records moved into acme's store and served by acme's search/sql. tenantPinnedStore() now suppresses the legacy identity whenever a tenant is selected. Found by the onboard Codex review (P1); TestTenantStoreNeverAdoptsBearerStore fails with the guard removed.

handfixes.summary: The client refuses to send an Authorization header over plain http to anything but a loopback host
handfixes.why: GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_BASE_URL (declared in the .mcpb for mock testing) can point at http://. The generated client attached the raw bearer or the tenant-minted token to the first request regardless of scheme; the redirect guards only cover later hops. A non-loopback http override therefore sent a super-admin-delegated token in cleartext. credentialWouldTravelInPlaintext now refuses before dialling, while http://127.0.0.1 and localhost mocks keep working. Found by the onboard Codex review (P1); receipt: http://192.0.2.10 is refused, the loopback stub still answers. The call-site test (TestClientRefusesCredentialOverPlaintext) fails with the guard removed; the helper-only test does not. Round 2 (Codex, P1): the first version also exempted *.localhost, but Go's environment proxy only exempts localhost and loopback IPs, so http://fixture.localhost with HTTP_PROXY set delivered the bearer header to the proxy. Only localhost and loopback IPs are exempt now. Round 3 (adversarial): the guard lower-cased the host, but Go's proxy match on localhost is case-exact, so http://LOCALHOST was exempt from the guard yet sent through HTTP_PROXY; the comparison is case-exact now.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generated clients should refuse credential-bearing non-loopback plaintext requests fleet-wide.

handfixes.summary: tenants test reports a fan-out worker that was cancelled or panicked as a failed tenant
handfixes.why: FanoutRun returns worker errors separately from results, and tenants test discarded them, so a cancelled or panicked worker vanished from the report and could not count toward the failure exit. Each FanoutError now becomes a failed tenantTestResult. Found by the onboard Codex review (P2). gws_tenants_cmd.go is a NOVEL file carried from the factory's novel/ directory.

handfixes.summary: sync treats a Google list page with no items array ({kind, etag}) as an empty page instead of storing the envelope as one record
handfixes.why: Google omits the items array when a list is empty. The generated sync loop falls through to 'single object response - store as-is' when it finds no items and isEmptyPageResponse does not recognise the envelope, so a tenant with no data transfers stored the {kind, etag} envelope as a transfer and reported total_records 1. All five synced resources are lists, so an item-less Google envelope is always an empty page. Found by the onboard Codex review (round 2, P1); receipt: a stub returning {kind, etag} for transfers stored 1 record before and 0 after. The helper lives in the hand-written gws_sync_envelope.go; the call site in sync.go is the generated-file edit.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the googlediscovery profiler should populate responsePathForResource with each list method's items key, and the sync loop should never store a list resource's page as a single object.

handfixes.summary: pageMayHaveMore treats a Google list envelope without nextPageToken as the proven last page
handfixes.why: With pagination now declared (sync-google-page-token-pagination), a final page of exactly maxResults records and no nextPageToken hit the generic 'full page without a usable next cursor' rule: sync emitted a false truncation warning and left the resource's completion unproven while still reporting success. In Google's list contract a missing nextPageToken is the end. Found by the onboard Codex review (round 2, P2); receipt: a stub returning exactly 100 users with no token warned pagination_cursor_missing before and completes cleanly after.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: treat a page_token paginator's absent next-token as a proven end when the response is an object envelope.

handfixes.summary: A selected client tenant always uses its own data-<hash>.db and never claims the shared, unscoped data.db
handfixes.why: The press's legacy-store migration lets the first scoped identity to find an existing data.db claim it (claimLegacyUnscopedDB writes data.db.owner). In this multi-tenant CLI data.db is what a read with no tenant selected opens, so whichever client synced first had its mirror served to every unscoped sql/search call: the adversarial reviewer synced acme then beta and an MCP sql call with GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_TENANT unset returned acme's users. defaultDBPathInDir now returns the tenant's scoped file before the claim step. Found by the onboard adversarial review (round 2, P1); TestTenantStoreNeverClaimsUnscopedDBAndLocalReadNeedsTenant fails with the guard removed.

handfixes.summary: Local-store reads (MCP sql/search, CLI search/analytics, --data-source local) refuse when tenants are registered, none is selected, and no bearer token keys the store
handfixes.why: With no tenant selected and no bearer token the store scope is empty and reads open the shared data.db, which holds no client's mirror, so an empty result reads as a clean one (no users without 2SV, no stale licences). localStoreTenantErr (novel gws_tenants.go) returns a usage error naming --tenant / GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_TENANT; a bearer token keys the store to its own organization, the same one generated API commands act on, so that case is allowed. Found by the onboard adversarial review (round 2, P1, with tenant-store-never-claims-unscoped-db). Round 17 (Codex P2): playbook list/amend, teach-playbook and the learnings candidates/stats commands still opened the store unguarded, so the guard moved into learnDBPath itself (it now returns an error) and the compiler names every opener; TestQuarantinedTenantLocalReadRefused fails with the guard removed. Round 18 (Codex + adversarial P2): the learn and playbook seed shims in PersistentPreRunE opened defaultDBPath directly; they now resolve through learnDBPath and skip when no unquarantined tenant store is selected.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Factory-side: carry localStoreTenantErr in ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/google-workspace/novel/gws_tenants.go; the four call sites are generated-file edits a reprint drops.

handfixes.summary: Novel-command help text says what the code does: offboard's order is 'safe' (not API-required) and its Example uses --json; posture and sharing-drift count every Drive/Calendar setting change, not only sharing; tenants add's mode 0600 applies on macOS/Linux
handfixes.why: The adversarial review (round 2, P2) and Codex (round 2, P1, Windows key ACLs) found help text that overclaimed: Google does not require offboard's order (backup-code invalidation failing on a suspended account is why suspend runs last), --agent's compact output drops each offboard step's detail, settingChanges keeps every CHANGE_DOCS_SETTING and CHANGE_CALENDAR_SETTING event, and on Windows the copied key inherits the config folder's ACL. These are NOVEL files carried from the factory's novel/ directory, so a re-onboard from that source brings the old text back. Round 3 (adversarial, P2) found the same 'sharing settings' text on the generated surfaces that carry the novel-feature list (root --help, which's curated index, the MCP context tool) and in posture's table column and JSON key, now SETTING_CHANGES and drive_calendar_setting_changes. Round 4 (adversarial and Codex, P2): the offboard 'in the order Google's API requires' text also survived on root --help, which and the MCP context tool.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Factory-side: port the same wording into ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/google-workspace/novel/ (offboard.go, posture.go, sharing_drift.go, gws_tenants_cmd.go).

asserts.not_contains: in the order the API requires

asserts.contains: any Drive (Docs) or Calendar setting changed in the Admin console

asserts.not_contains: in the order Google's API requires
in the order Google's API requires
in the order Google's API requires

handfixes.summary: Each MCP tool call re-reads the tenant registry (RefreshTenantSelection in MCPStorePath and newMCPClient), so a long-running server stops auto-selecting the only tenant once a second one is registered; a CLI command still resolves its tenant once
handfixes.why: selectedTenant cached its first answer for the life of the process. The MCP server is long-lived (Claude Desktop, --transport http), and tenants are added from a terminal because tenants add is not exposed over MCP. A server that had auto-selected the only tenant kept serving it after a second was registered: sql returned the first client's rows, search returned a clean-looking zero for the second client, and the raw execute tool kept minting the first client's token (adversarial review round 3, P1). The first fix re-resolved whenever tenants.toml changed, but that let one CLI command open one client's store in its pre-run and then authenticate as another client if the registry changed mid-run (Codex round 4, P1). Selection is now stable for a process and refreshed explicitly at each MCP tool call's entry, so every CLI command and every MCP call sees one tenant throughout. TestTenantSelectionFollowsRegistryChanges checks both halves and fails with the MCPStorePath refresh removed. Round 5 (Codex, P1): with the HTTP transport serving calls concurrently, one call's refresh could land between another call's tenant guard and its store path; mcpTenantMu now serializes RefreshTenantSelection and the whole MCPStorePath sequence.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Factory-side: carry RefreshTenantSelection into ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/google-workspace/novel/gws_tenants.go; the two call sites are generated-file edits a reprint drops.

handfixes.summary: A tenant's local store is keyed to its name AND domain
handfixes.why: Keyed to the name alone, removing a tenant and registering the same name for a different client reopened the previous client's mirror and later syncs mixed both clients' records. A Google Workspace primary domain identifies the client, so it is part of the key; changing a tenant's scopes with tenants add --yes keeps the same store. Found by the onboard Codex review (round 3, P1).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Factory-side: carry tenantStoreIdentity into the factory's novel/gws_tenants.go.

handfixes.summary: When the config file fails to load, a selected tenant keeps its own store scope instead of falling back to the shared data.db; localStoreTenantErr also refuses if a selected tenant's scope is not the current one
handfixes.why: configureDefaultDBScope cleared the store scope on any config.Load error, which sends every store open to the unscoped data.db, possibly another organization's bearer-mode mirror, while localStoreTenantErr allowed the read because a tenant was selected. A tenant's store does not depend on the config file, so the scope is computed from an empty config (the tenant hook still applies), and the read guard checks that the active scope is the selected tenant's. Found by the onboard Codex review (round 3, P1); the malformed-config phase of TestTenantSelectionFollowsRegistryChanges fails with the old line.

handfixes.summary: export and tail read Google lists properly: the read configs carry each list's items key and pageToken/nextPageToken paging, an item-less Google envelope is an empty page, and both send the list's spec defaults (customer=my_customer for users and groups)
handfixes.why: The Discovery print left resourceReadConfigs empty, so export wrote the first Google envelope as one record and never followed nextPageToken (Codex round 3, P1: incomplete backups that exit 0), wrote a {kind, etag} envelope for an empty list, and sent no customer parameter, which Google requires for users.list and groups.list. Receipts against a two-page stub: export users wrote 1 line before and 130 after, export transfers on an empty list writes nothing, and both requests now carry customer=my_customer. Round 4 (Codex, P1): tail still read only the first page per poll; fetchAndEmit now follows nextPageToken through fetchAndEmitPage (receipt: 130 events over two stub pages).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the googlediscovery profiler should fill resourceReadConfigs (responsePath, cursor paging) and export/tail should seed the same spec defaults sync does.

handfixes.summary: The MCP sql and search tool descriptions say they read one client tenant's mirror (GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_TENANT or the only registered tenant) and refuse when several are registered and none is set; the MCP context tool's tips describe Google's pageToken/maxResults paging and drop the generic message/channel playbook entries
handfixes.why: The generated descriptions said 'across all synced data', but in this multi-tenant CLI they read exactly one tenant's store and take no tenant argument, which an MCP-only agent (Claude Desktop, ChatGPT) cannot learn from human docs. Found by the onboard adversarial review (round 3, P2). The generated prefixes are kept because tools_test.go pins them. Round 4 (adversarial, P2): the context tool, which agents are told to call first, still carried generic archetype tips (an 'after' cursor and a pageSize parameter no command takes, and message/channel playbooks for data this connector never syncs). Round 5 (adversarial, P2): the paging tip now tells the agent to re-request a page that came back _pp_truncated (MCP execute cuts responses at 60 KB but keeps nextPageToken) with a smaller maxResults before moving on.

asserts.contains: of one client tenant: the GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_TENANT tenant, or the only registered one
If a response carries _pp_truncated, the page was cut to fit

handfixes.summary: The per-tenant token-source cache is keyed to the service-account key's content as well as tenant, admin and scopes
handfixes.why: Keyed to name, admin and scopes only, a long-running MCP server kept refreshing tokens through a source built from the old key after the operator rotated it with tenants add --yes, until restart; once the old key is revoked every call fails. The key file is read on each lookup (a few KB) and its SHA-256 prefix joins the cache key. Found by the onboard Codex review (round 4, P1); TestTokenSourceFollowsKeyRotation fails with the hash removed.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Factory-side: carry the key-content cache key into the factory's novel/gws_tenants.go.

handfixes.summary: The 400/401/403 auth hints name --tenant / GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_TENANT (or the selected tenant's delegation and scopes) when client tenants are registered, and the bearer-token line only when none are; the MCP execute tool appends the same hint to 401/403 errors, and the MCP context tool's auth section names GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_TENANT and scopes the bearer tokens to single-organization use; a Google quota/rate 403 is classified as a rate limit, not a permission problem; agent-context .auth and guide.md's env table name GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_TENANT
handfixes.why: The generated hints always said to export GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_TOKEN, while the docs say to unset it once tenants are registered. With several tenants and none selected, a generated command goes out with no credential and the hint pointed the user, or an MCP agent, at the wrong fix. Found by the onboard adversarial review (round 4, P2). Round 5 (adversarial, P2): the in-process MCP execute tool returned the raw 401 and the context tool listed only the bearer tokens ('Set to your API credential'), so an MCP-only agent still had no path to the tenant fix. Round 6: the MCP execute 403 hint in single-organization mode told the agent to set the token it had already sent (adversarial, P2); a quota 403 (rateLimitExceeded and similar) got credential advice (Codex, P2); the CLI agent-context twin of the MCP context auth section still listed only the bearer tokens (adversarial, P2).

handfixes.summary: groups list sends its default customer=my_customer only when no --user-key is given
handfixes.why: Google's groups.list rejects customer together with userKey, and the generated command always sent the flag's my_customer default, so 'groups list --user-key <email>' (a user's group memberships) failed. An explicitly set --customer is still sent. Found by the onboard Codex review (round 4, P2); receipt: the stub now sees ?userKey=... alone, and ?customer=my_customer without --user-key.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: Discovery marks customer/domain/userKey as alternatives; the generator should not default one when another is supplied.

handfixes.summary: A tenant-bound client asks the tenant's auto-refreshing token source for the Authorization value on every request (Config.AuthHeaderSource), instead of a token minted once at client build
handfixes.why: bindTenantToken stored the minted token as a static Authorization value, so any run longer than Google's one-hour token lifetime (tail --follow, a large sync) kept sending an expired token and every later call failed 401 while 'tenants test' passed. AuthHeaderSource is consulted first by Config.AuthHeader(), which the request path and the output credential masking both use, so a refreshed token is also masked. Found by the onboard adversarial review (round 5, P2: a 12-second-token stub showed tail re-using an expired token) and Codex (round 5, P1); TestTenantTokenRefreshesPerRequest fails with the AuthHeader() check removed. The field sits at the end of the generated Config struct so gofmt leaves the rest aligned.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: config.Config could offer a token-source hook for prints whose auth layer mints short-lived tokens.

handfixes.summary: Secret-named query parameters are masked everywhere the client masks credential text (error URLs, dry-run lines, bodies), and --dry-run body previews redact every non-empty, non-boolean secret-named field (password, secret, private key, API key, *token except page/sync tokens)
handfixes.why: The generated dry-run printer wrote the request body verbatim to stderr, so previewing 'users patch <email> --password ...' put the password into the terminal and into agent transcripts. Found by the onboard Codex review (round 5, P1); receipt: the real binary's dry-run of users patch --password prints "password": "[redacted]" and the value appears nowhere in stdout or stderr. Round 6 (Codex): query parameters were still printed verbatim (subscriptions insert --customer-auth-token showed the transfer token; P1, also fleet-wide generated code), and the body rule hid the changePasswordAtNextLogin boolean (P2). Receipt: the dry-run now prints ?customerAuthToken=[redacted]. Round 7 (Codex, P1, fleet): a failed request's error message carried the full URL, so MCP execute of subscriptions.insert returned customerAuthToken verbatim; redactSecretQueryParams now runs inside maskCredentialText, which every error, URL and body passes through (receipt: the MCP error reads ?customerAuthToken=[redacted]). The adversarial reviewer also noted string-only body redaction let a numeric password or a 'Secrets' custom-schema object through; only booleans stay visible now. Round 8 (Codex, P1, fleet): the dry-run body bypassed maskCredentialText, so users watch --address 'https://hooks.example/?token=...' printed the webhook secret; the body text now goes through the mask (HTML escaping off so & stays literal), printing ?token=[redacted]. Round 11 (Codex, P1): the value pattern stopped at a quote, so ?token='SECRET' (and a JSON-escaped \"SECRET\") slipped through, and \u0026 / & separators were not recognised; the pattern now allows an opening (escaped) quote and those separators, and RedactURLSecrets also masks a userinfo password (https://user:pass@host). Round 12 (adversarial P2s): an empty value followed by its closing quote is left alone (the dry-run JSON stays valid); userinfo is split like net/url (password runs to the last @ before / ? #, quotes and @ allowed); sig= and code= are secret names (SAS and Azure Functions webhook signatures). TestRedactSecretQueryParams covers each case and the non-secret texts that must stay unchanged. Round 13 (Codex P1s): the empty-quoted-value exception applies only when the whole value is separators, so ?token=';SECRET' is masked; names containing 'signature' (X-Amz-Signature, X-Goog-Signature) are secret; and the client's request-build error (a URL that fails to parse, e.g. a base URL with user:pass@ and a bad escape) goes through maskCredentialText. TestRequestBuildErrorMasksURLSecrets fails without it. Round 14 (Codex P1s): the value is now found by a scanner instead of a regex: the URL's enclosing quote (nearest quote before the URL with no whitespace between) closes an empty value, another opening quote runs to its match, and an unquoted value may contain an apostrophe (?token=O'Hara-SECRET was half-printed); bare key= is a secret name (Google API keys); doctor's base_url and feedback --send errors are masked. TestRedactSecretQueryParams covers each case, including JSON arrays with an empty secret value. Round 15 (adversarial P1 + P2s): the enclosing quote is the character before the URL's scheme, looked up within a 2 KiB window, so an earlier apostrophe in the URL no longer acts as the enclosing quote (?name=O'Hara&token=... leaked), a quote-led secret right after the URL's own quote is masked, an empty value at the end of a JSON string with text before the URL keeps the JSON valid, and a megabyte of parameters stays linear. Round 16 (adversarial P2s): a quoted value runs to its closing quote across spaces and & (it stops at a line break, a bare " or 2 KiB, so it never crosses JSON structure). Round 17 (Codex P2): with no enclosing quote, a double quote after = followed by any punctuation counted as an empty value, so ?token=";SECRET" printed and profile save stored it; the quote now ends an empty value only when JSON structure follows (end, } or ], or a comma then a key, object or array). Round 18 (Codex + adversarial P2): a closing } or ] counts as JSON structure only when the end or a comma follows (so ?token="}SECRET is masked), and hyphenated names (x-api-key, private-key) are secret. Accepted: a value that itself begins "," followed by a quote, or "" then text, is read as empty; real URL secrets are percent-encoded tokens and API query values are percent-encoded by the client.

handfixes.summary: posture resolves Cloud Identity policies the way Google does (all three columns use the Max reducer): within one applicability scope (the policy CEL query, which carries org unit, group and licence conditions; orgUnit/group when the query is absent) the policy with the greatest sortOrder wins, and a field it omits takes Google's documented default (external_sharing_mode ALLOWED, enable_auto_forwarding true, enforced_from unset); mixed:... appears only when scopes resolve differently
handfixes.why: summarizePolicyValues collapsed every returned policy into a set of values, so a SYSTEM default (ALLOWED) overridden by an ADMIN policy (DISALLOWED) for the same users read mixed:ALLOWED,DISALLOWED, telling an MSP a client had differing sharing settings it does not have. Google documents the reduction (https://docs.cloud.google.com/identity/docs/concepts/policy-api-concepts): filter to the policies that apply, then the greatest sortOrder wins. Found by the onboard Codex review (round 17, P1). posture.go is a NOVEL file carried from the factory novel/ directory. Ceiling: scopes are not resolved against the OU tree, so mixed means the scopes differ. TestSummarizePolicyValues fails with the sortOrder comparison removed. Round 18 (Codex P1 x2): skipping a winning policy that omits the field kept a lower policy's value (Max takes the default instead), and keying on orgUnit/group merged licence-scoped policies for different users; the scope is now the query and each column carries its documented default. handfixes.summary: verification-codes list bypasses the on-disk HTTP response cache, so a user's live backup codes are never written under the cache dir
handfixes.why: The generated read path caches every GET response as JSON under the cache dir (0600) until a later write clears it, so verification-codes list left a user's live 2SV backup codes on disk. The fleet template does the same for every connector (hudu, itglue cache passwords), so it is P2 under the fleet rule, but a one-line NoCache on this command removes the copy. handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names.
